note: Credit and provenance for every file under ui/assets-gothic/. The gothic concept and all of its artwork was generated with ChatGPT (OpenAI) across several sessions, for the Pilgrim project. No third party requires attribution, but the record is kept in the same machine-readable shape as ui/assets/attribution.json so the same tooling can read it. Do not describe any of this artwork as manually illustrated.
reproducibility: The originals cannot be regenerated. They came out of ChatGPT sessions with no prompt or seed on record, and image generation is not deterministic anyway, so a lost original is lost -- asking again produces different artwork, not the same artwork. Files marked reproducibleBy can be rebuilt from the originals by that script; everything else is an original in its own right and its only copy is the one in this repository.

grounds/candidates/planks_rough_ringed.p.role:
THE EVIDENCE FOR A RECORDED NUMBER, and the only file in this tree kept for that reason. It is grounds/planks_rough.png before the measuring ring was stripped: 1448 x 1086 with the ring on it, where the filed plate is 1170 x 577 and has none.

IT IS NOT A CANDIDATE, despite the folder. It sits here because candidates/ is beside the plate and is not scanned by generate_asset_check's ground panel, which globs grounds/*.png and would otherwise report a ring-bearing image as a seventh plate. It is not an alternative to planks_rough.png; it IS planks_rough.png, one step earlier.

WHAT IT SETTLES. duty_grounds.json records a camera of 31.14 degrees for planks_rough, read off this ring rather than off the plate's own outline, because a ragged patch of plank ends is not an ellipse and fitting one to it reads 30.66 -- the fit visibly bulges past the timber on one side and falls inside it on the other. Until this file was recovered, that 31.14 could not be re-derived from anything in the repository, which made it the one number here no later measurement could contradict. It now re-derives exactly: sculpt_metrics.ring_ellipse fits 31.1400 degrees at a ratio of 0.5171, and the plate's own outline reads 30.6589, agreeing to 0.4811 -- inside the 1.5 a candidate's ring and outline must agree within. An independent measurement made the same day with a different implementation (OpenCV's fitEllipse rather than this project's numpy SVD conic fit) returned 0.5173 and 31.15.

THE IDENTITY IS PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED. Strip the ring from this file and crop to its ink and the result is byte-for-byte identical to the committed grounds/planks_rough.png -- every channel of every pixel, mean absolute difference 0.000. Nine other images from the same batch were checked as controls; one matched on size and differed in content, the rest differed in size.

WHY IT NEARLY DID NOT SURVIVE. The practice was strip-then-file, with the ring discarded as a jig. That is right for a plate whose own outline can be measured and wrong for one carrying a recorded camera, where the ring is the measurement. The original was gone from disk by 2026-09-24 and was recovered only because the generating session could still be found. The rule this establishes: a plate that needs a camera block gets its ring-bearing source filed beside it, asserted by test_a_recorded_camera_keeps_the_ring_it_was_read_from.
